item.title: TMG/Betaine (Trimethylglycine)
item.description:
What it is: TMG (Trimethylglycine), also called betaine, is a methyl donor compound essential for methylation—a fundamental biochemical process underlying detoxification, energy production, and gene expression. TMG supplementation supports cardiovascular health via homocysteine reduction, cellular energy, and longevity pathways.

What Is TMG/Betaine?

TMG is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative found in beets, spinach, whole grains, and seafood. It contains three methyl groups (-CH3) that it donates to metabolic processes, making it a critical methyl donor in the body.

item.title: L-Carnitine
item.description:
What it is: L-Carnitine is a naturally occurring amino acid that transports long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for oxidation into energy. Essential for fat metabolism and ATP production, it’s particularly valuable for athletes, aging populations, and those optimizing body composition without the stimulant side effects of other fat-loss supplements.

What Is L-Carnitine?

L-Carnitine is a quaternary amine compound synthesized in the body from amino acids lysine and methionine. While your body produces carnitine naturally (about 1-2 grams daily), dietary sources are limited, and supplementation can increase carnitine availability significantly—particularly for those with high metabolic demands.

item.title: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B12?

Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a unique water-soluble vitamin containing cobalt at its center — the only vitamin containing a metal. B12 serves as a critical cofactor in just two major enzymes, but these enzymes catalyze absolutely essential reactions affecting energy production, DNA synthesis, neurological function, and the methylation cycle.

Biochemistry: B12 exists in several forms. The two primary active forms in the body are:

  • Methylcobalamin: Methyl donor form; directly supports the methylation cycle (methionine synthase)
  • Adenosylcobalamin (AdoCB12): Energy metabolism form; cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase

item.title: CoQ10
item.description:
What Is CoQ10?

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), also called ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring coenzyme found in every cell in your body. It’s essential for:

  1. ATP Production — the energy currency of cells
  2. Antioxidant Defense — protecting cells from oxidative damage
  3. Cellular Signaling — regulating important biological processes

While your body produces CoQ10, production declines with age (dropping 50% by age 60) and is depleted by certain medications, particularly statins.

CoQ10 is especially critical for high-energy organs: the heart, brain, liver, and kidneys.

item.title: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
item.description:
What Is PQQ?

Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a small quinone molecule that functions as a powerful redox cofactor and cellular signaling compound. First discovered in bacteria in 1979, PQQ has emerged as one of the most exciting longevity and cognitive enhancement compounds in biohacking circles.

PQQ is unique among supplements because it:

  1. Stimulates Mitochondrial Biogenesis — the creation of entirely new mitochondria
  2. Functions as a Potent Antioxidant — up to 5,000 redox cycles vs. 4 for vitamin C
  3. Activates Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) — supporting neuroplasticity and brain health
  4. Protects Neurons — from oxidative stress and excitotoxicity

PQQ is considered a novel vitamin-like compound: While not yet classified as an essential vitamin, research suggests PQQ may be conditionally essential for optimal human function.
